statusText: Tail lifts to 14%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The 05:16Z retracement to 31,409.75 failed and NQ Dec26 extended to a new session low of 31,313.50, trading 31,316.75 and holding near that low, while Stress rises to 55% with Brent at 102.75 near its session high and the 10-year close to a 24-year high.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains EA_ON with Tail at 14%, below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30Z-15:00Z around the US cash open, where conditional Tail reaches a 22% WATCH peak. Jobless claims at 12:30Z and the 17:00Z 30-year Treasury auction are the session's other checkpoints, the auction more pointed than usual with the long end near multi-decade highs.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures set a new session low as a failed retracement meets firmer crude and a long end near 24-year highs
body: The seventh Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session has reversed the recovery flagged an hour earlier. NQ Dec26 trades 31,316.75 at 06:17Z, -85.50 or -0.27% against a 31,402.25 prior close, and a second independent quote put it at 31,337.00 at about 06:10Z, so the direction is confirmed across sources. The 05:16Z retracement to 31,409.75 failed: price has since extended through the earlier 31,349.50 low to a new session low of 31,313.50 and is holding within roughly 25 points of it. The session band is 31,313.50-31,466.00, or 152.5 points and 0.49%. A failed retracement followed by extension to a new low, with price holding near that extreme, is the structure the Tail score is built to detect, and it is why Tail lifts from 11% to 14% and the dominant mode moves to trend-down. What keeps the score far below the blocking threshold is magnitude: the whole move is 0.27% inside a 0.49% band, VIX closed Oct 7 at 15.08 with no evidence of a volatility regime shift, and the long end is stable today at 5.28-5.30% rather than extending toward the 5.326% overnight high or the 5.365% Oct 7 intraday peak. Asian cash confirms the tilt without matching the extreme. The Nikkei 225 trades 69,390.74, -0.92%, having given back the recovery seen an hour earlier but still about 197 points above its 69,194.12 low; AP reporting timed at 05:17Z put the Kospi 0.8% lower at 6,750.25, the Taiex down 0.7%, the Hang Seng 0.2% lower at 24,072.98 and the Shanghai Composite 0.1% down at 3,840.03. The Oct 7 cash session closed with the Nasdaq-100 at 31,160.08, -0.21%. Energy is the clearest aligned pressure: Brent trades 102.75, +2.55 or +2.54%, in a 100.75-102.92 range, so crude sits near its session high while equities sit at their low. The catalyst is a report that the White House asked the Pentagon to prepare Iran strike options executable before the November midterms, together with Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks at their highest weekly level since the conflict began, a tanker struck off Qatar with casualties, and more than 510,000 barrels per day shut in by Tropical Storm Isaias. Offsetting that, Gulf crude exports are estimated near 98% of pre-conflict levels, the G7 agreed a 100-million-barrel emergency release and OPEC+ left quotas unchanged, which is why this remains a Stress and gap-risk input rather than an observed one-way equity path. The AI-linked debt wave persists as a credit-channel risk to megacap technology: Broadcom is reported to be seeking about $50bn of financing, SpaceX roughly $30bn of investment-grade debt plus $10bn of loans to buy Nvidia chips with its credit-default insurance at record highs, and Oracle is also reported to be raising for AI chips. The dollar index near 102.22 sits close to an 18-month high, and the September FOMC minutes record most participants seeing another increase as likely by year end from the current 3.75-4.00%. Under the risk contract this stack lifts Stress to 55% and leaves Tail at 14%, because aligned background pressure is not the same as observed persistent one-way NQ structure. Shared Finviz context was read and found stale, dated 2026-09-29 with partial collection status, so it was excluded and the assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 10-14% through the Asian and European hours of Oct 7, rose into a 20-23% WATCH band between 11:00Z and 15:00Z as a trend-down phase developed into the US cash open, then decayed steadily once the dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into the close. Every hour from 16:00Z onward held 10-18% in the EA_ON band. Stress ranged 47-54% across the window and ended at 53% as long-end yields and crude firmed, while Confidence held 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: Base case is two-way NQ rotation resuming after the current downward tilt, while firmer crude near $102.75, a 10-year close to a 24-year high, a dollar index at an 18-month peak and AI-linked technology debt stress remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail holds 14% through the late Asian hours, firms to 15-16% across the European session and the 08:30Z Waller speech, rises to 19% in the hour containing the 12:30Z jobless claims release and peaks at 22% WATCH in the hour containing the 13:30Z US cash open, eases to 18-19% through the US morning, holds 19% for the 17:00Z 30-year auction and 17:40Z Musalem speech, then decays to 11-17% across the Globex and Asian hours into the Oct 9 European pre-open. Confidence declines from 88% to 76% with forecast distance only.
